interest: Although consisting of cross-reference sheets pointing to the primary record in decimal file 811d.0144/2, this file illuminates rising Japanese-American military tensions in the western Pacific less than six months before the attack on Pearl Harbor and the invasion of Guam. It provides documentary evidence of unauthorized Japanese aerial reconnaissance missions probing American defenses on Guam, and demonstrates the U.S. Navy Department's urging of diplomatic intervention via the State Department to formally protest these violations to Tokyo.
overview: This file (894.2311D) contains State Department cross-reference sheets dated June 19, 1941, regarding unauthorized flights of Japanese aircraft over the U.S. island territory of Guam. The referenced correspondence originated from the Navy Department, which requested that the matter be formally brought to the attention of the Japanese Government. The underlying primary letter is indexed under State Department file 811d.0144/2, reflecting military surveillance and territorial airspace concerns in the Pacific in the months preceding the outbreak of World War II.

subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet records a letter dated June 19, 1941, from the Navy Department to the Department of State regarding unauthorized flights of Japanese aircraft over Guam. The Navy Department requested that the attention of the Japanese Government be directed to these incursions. The original letter was filed under decimal file 811d.0144/2, and this reference sheet bears the initials FLH.
